source: The east entrance will close at 4:30 p.m. on Thursday while the handrail is repaired. Please use the courtyard entrance after that time. The lift will remain available, and deliveries can still reach the loading bay. We expect the repair to take one evening; we will post an update if that changes.

source: I left your blue bowl on the kitchen shelf, beside the tea. Thanks for lending it to me. The soup survived the bus ride, which is more than I can say for my umbrella. No rush to pick it up; I can bring it over when we meet on Sunday.

source: The pilot measured how often visitors used the new labels, not whether the labels improved recall. Participants chose their own routes through the gallery, so exposure varied. These results describe engagement within this sample. They do not establish that the same labels would change learning outcomes in a different exhibition.
objective: Review this research limitation paragraph for clear wording while retaining the distinction between engagement and learning.

source: Dad, the little radio works again. The loose wire was under the battery tray, so the fix took less time than finding my screwdriver. I kept the sticker that says “DO NOT BIN.” It looks slightly grumpy on the windowsill, which seems right. Call when you have a minute and I will play you the weather forecast.
objective: Polish this family message only where it helps readability. Keep the joke and the exact sticker wording “DO NOT BIN.”

source: Volunteer briefing: Saturday, 18 April, at 9:00 a.m. in the ferry terminal classroom. Please arrive ten minutes early so we can distribute name badges before the session begins. The briefing covers radio use, visitor questions, and the procedure for reporting a lost item. You do not need previous harbour experience to attend. Bring a reusable cup if you would like tea or coffee. We will supply printed maps and pencils. After the briefing, anyone who wants to can join a short walk along the public pier. The walk is optional and does not count toward the training requirement. If you cannot attend, email the volunteer desk so we can send you the next available date. Please avoid replying to the entire mailing list.
objective: Update the briefing date to Saturday, 25 April, and the start time to 10:00 a.m. Keep all other instructions and details as written.

source: Your seed exchange reservation is confirmed for table C7. The reservation includes one table, two chairs, and a small sign holder. Doors open to exhibitors at 8:15 a.m.; visitors enter at 9:00 a.m. Please label each packet with the plant name and the year the seeds were collected. The organisers cannot verify every packet, so avoid making guarantees about germination. Swaps are welcome, but selling seeds is not permitted during this event. If you bring plants in pots, place a tray beneath them to protect the floor. A trolley will be available at the side entrance. Return it promptly so another exhibitor can use it. We look forward to seeing your collection and hearing the stories behind it.
objective: Change the reservation to table D3 and change the included chairs from two to three. Preserve the rest of the confirmation, including the limits on sales and germination claims.

source: Dear Members, our winter borrowing allowance is eight tools per household. Tools may be kept for fourteen days, and renewals are available if nobody else has requested the item. Please return each tool clean and with any supplied attachments. Staff will inspect electrical items before lending them again. A damaged item should be handed directly to the desk rather than placed in the return cabinet. Reporting damage does not automatically result in a charge; we first check what happened and whether the issue arose through normal use. You can reserve tools through the catalogue or ask a volunteer to help during opening hours. Membership cards remain valid until their printed expiry date. Thank you for helping us keep the collection useful and safe for everyone.
objective: Update the winter borrowing allowance to six tools per household and the loan period to twenty-one days. Make only those factual updates and any grammar adjustments they require.

source: Workshop reminder: the felt repair session takes place in Room Alder. Your booking includes a starter kit with grey wool, two needles, and a foam pad. We will practise on sample fabric before working on anything you bring from home. Please choose an item with a small worn area rather than a large tear, since the session is designed for beginners. The tutor can suggest an approach but cannot promise an invisible repair. If you prefer to watch the demonstration without attempting a repair, you are welcome to do so. Keep your booking email handy at the entrance. There is no need to print it. The community cafe opens before the session, although refreshments are not included in the booking price.
objective: Replace Room Alder with Room Willow and replace grey wool with navy wool in the starter kit description. Leave the rest of the reminder intact.

source: The archive reading room is open to registered visitors. You can request up to four boxes for each visit, and staff will bring them to your assigned desk. Please use a pencil when taking notes near original material. There is no restriction on using a laptop, provided its case is left in the locker area. The booking form asks whether you need an accessible desk; answering this question helps us arrange the room before you arrive. Staff are on hand in order to provide assistance with locating catalogue entries. They cannot conduct a full search on your behalf during a reading room appointment. If you need more time, book another visit rather than reserving additional places under a different name. Copies may be requested after you have reviewed the material.
objective: Simplify only the sentence beginning “Staff are on hand”. Keep the surrounding notice and its boundaries on research assistance unchanged.

source: In this exercise, groups compared two sets of fictional interview transcripts. One set included pauses marked in brackets; the other presented only spoken words. Students were asked to identify places where they wanted more context, rather than to assign a confidence score to the speaker. The exercise was an opportunity to engage in the undertaking of a discussion about transcription choices. Several groups noticed that punctuation could imply a stronger conclusion than the recorded words supported. Others focused on how the removal of repetition changed the rhythm of a reply. These observations were collected on paper at the end of the class. They were not graded, and no attempt was made to rank the two transcript formats. A later session will examine how different transcription conventions handle overlapping speech.
objective: Replace the cumbersome sentence about the opportunity for discussion with a clear, ordinary sentence. Edit that sentence only and retain the exercise's limited purpose.
